new_candidates.body:
### Intro

I am an undergrad student at University of Montreal, I use MuJoCo and MJX for my research on robot learning.

### My setup

MuJoCo `main` at f0b3de317, with `libmujoco` built from that commit and MJX from the same tree. Python API, Python 3.14, JAX 0.11.1 on CPU, x86_64, Ubuntu 26.04 on WSL2.

### What's happening? What did you expect?

An MJX contact sensor with `reduce="none"`, the default, reports `force`, `torque`, `dist`, `pos`, `normal` and `tangent` from the wrong contact. `found` is correct, so the readings look valid.

In the model below, spheres `b` and `c` touch the floor and sphere `a` does not. Sensors on `b` and `c` report `found=1`, force 0 and dist 0.4. Those are the values of `a`, 0.4 above the floor.

I expected the behaviour in the [XML reference](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/latest/XMLreference.html#sensor-contact): "Returns the first num contacts that satisfy the matching criterion, in the order that they appear in mjData.contact". MuJoCo C reports force 143.757 and dist -0.01 for `b`, and force 562.636 and dist -0.05 for `c`.

The cause is in `_sensor_contact._reduce` in `mjx/mujoco/mjx/_src/sensor.py`. For `reduce="none"` it returns `jp.arange(mask.size)` and ignores the mask, so the slots read the first `num` entries of the contact array. In MJX that array has a fixed size and also holds inactive candidates and the contacts of other geoms. `nfound` does use the match and active state, which is why `found` differs from the other fields.

This affects models that read values through a contact sensor with the default `reduce`, for example the force on a foot geom, unless the matching active contact happens to be in the first slot. `doc/mjx.rst` tells users to read contacts solely through contact sensors. Gradients are affected too: for `<contact geom1="b" data="found dist"/>`, `jax.jacfwd` with respect to the height of `b` gives 0 for `dist`, and 1 once the slot holds the contact of `b`.

`reduce="mindist"` and `reduce="maxforce"` sort by the mask and are not affected in this way. `test_sensor_contact` and `test_sensor_contact_velocity` only cover those two.

### Steps for reproduction

1. Load the model below.
2. Run the code below.
3. See `found=1` with force 0 and dist 0.4 for `geom_b` and `geom_c`.

### Minimal model for reproduction

<details>
<summary>minimal XML</summary>

```XML
<mujoco>
  <worldbody>
    <geom name="floor" type="plane" size="5 5 .1"/>
    <body pos="0 0 .5"><freejoint/><geom name="a" size=".1"/></body>
    <body pos="1 0 .09"><freejoint/><geom name="b" size=".1"/></body>
    <body pos="2 0 .05"><freejoint/><geom name="c" size=".1"/></body>
  </worldbody>
  <sensor>
    <contact name="any" data="found force dist"/>
    <contact name="geom_b" geom1="b" data="found force dist"/>
    <contact name="geom_c" geom1="c" data="found force dist"/>
  </sensor>
</mujoco>
```
</details>

### Code required for reproduction

```python
import jax, mujoco, numpy as np
from mujoco import mjx

np.set_printoptions(suppress=True)
XML = """
<mujoco>
  <worldbody>
    <geom name="floor" type="plane" size="5 5 .1"/>
    <body pos="0 0 .5"><freejoint/><geom name="a" size=".1"/></body>
    <body pos="1 0 .09"><freejoint/><geom name="b" size=".1"/></body>
    <body pos="2 0 .05"><freejoint/><geom name="c" size=".1"/></body>
  </worldbody>
  <sensor>
    <contact name="any" data="found force dist"/>
    <contact name="geom_b" geom1="b" data="found force dist"/>
    <contact name="geom_c" geom1="c" data="found force dist"/>
  </sensor>
</mujoco>
"""
m = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_string(XML)
d = mujoco.MjData(m)
dx = mjx.put_data(m, d)
mujoco.mj_forward(m, d)
dx = jax.jit(mjx.forward)(mjx.put_model(m), dx)
print(f'{"sensor":8} {"":8} found, force_x, force_y, force_z, dist')
for i in range(m.nsensor):
  a, n = m.sensor_adr[i], m.sensor_dim[i]
  print(f'{m.sensor(i).name:8} expected', np.round(d.sensordata[a:a+n], 3))
  print(f'{"":8} actual  ', np.round(np.asarray(dx.sensordata)[a:a+n], 3))
```

Output:

```text
sensor            found, force_x, force_y, force_z, dist
any      expected [  2.    143.757   0.      0.     -0.01 ]
         actual   [2.  0.  0.  0.  0.4]
geom_b   expected [  1.    143.757   0.     -0.     -0.01 ]
         actual   [1.  0.  0.  0.  0.4]
geom_c   expected [  1.    562.636   0.     -0.     -0.05 ]
         actual   [1.  0.  0.  0.  0.4]
```

Sorting on the match and active state instead of returning `arange` makes all three sensors match MuJoCo C. I can open a PR for this.

### Confirmations

- [x] I searched the [latest documentation](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/latest/overview.html) thoroughly before posting.
- [x] I searched previous [Issues](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/issues) and [Discussions](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/discussions), I am certain this has not been raised before.
new_candidates.title: [MJX] Contact sensor with reduce="none" reports values from unmatched contacts

### Description The Mermaid diagram under "Kit decision tree" in `skills/isaac-sim-validator/SKILL.md` doesn't render on GitHub. It shows "Parse error on line 3". **Cause:** the Reject labels have quotes partway through the label, for example `C[Reject: "No script provided"]`, and Mermaid can't parse that. **Fix:** wrap each whole label in quotes: ``` B -->|No| C["Reject: No script provided"] ``` The same change applies to all ten Reject labels in that block. I reproduced the error locally with mermaid-cli and confirmed the fix renders cleanly (image below). The skills folder is outside the external PR scope in CONTRIBUTING.md, so I'm filing an issue instead of a PR. One other observation: - The "Python?" node has a Yes branch but no No branch. Is that intentional?
Fixed diagram, rendered
### Isaac Sim version 6.2.0-rc.14 (release/6.3, default branch; also present on main) ### Operating System (OS) N/A (doc rendering issue, seen on github.com) ### GPU Name N/A ### GPU Driver and CUDA versions N/A ### Logs ```txt Error: Parse error on line 3: ... -->|No| C[Reject: "No script provided"] -----------------------^ Expecting 'SQE', 'DOUBLECIRCLEEND', 'PE', '-)', 'STADIUMEND', 'SUBROUTINEEND', 'PIPE', 'CYLINDEREND', 'DIAMOND_STOP', 'TAGEND', 'TRAPEND', 'INVTRAPEND', 'UNICODE_TEXT', 'TEXT', 'TAGSTART', got 'STR' ``` ### Additional information _No response_
